chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Hamza al-Thumali said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who said to another man, 'Write to my wife regarding her divorce, or write to my slave regarding his manumission; will that be a divorce or manumission?' He said, 'It will not be a divorce nor manumission until his tongue speaks it or his hand writes it, and he intends by it the divorce or manumission, and that is done by him with witnesses and he is absent from his family.' And agency in divorce is valid, and that which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.يَخُطَّهُ بِيَدِهِ: He writes it with his hand

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a written divorce to be considered valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that mere written instruction is insufficient; validity requires the husband's direct verbal pronouncement or personal handwriting, coupled with specific intention (niyyah) and the presence of witnesses during his absence from his family. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the husband's active agency in divorce, while simultaneously affirming the permissibility of agency (wakalah), a point supported by the subsequent narration referenced in the text.
